content.title: US Plans 85 F-35 Jets Under $1.5 Trillion Defence Budget, Reversing Last Year’s Procurement Cut
content.text: DefenceUS Plans 85 F-35 Jets Under $1.5 Trillion Defence Budget, Reversing Last Year’s Procurement CutSwarajya StaffApr 04, 2026 | Updated 12:21 PM GMT+5:30Save & read from anywhere!Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app.Sign InPreferPreferLockheed Martin F-35 (Representative image) (Website/Lockheed Martin)The Pentagon has reportedly requested 85 Lockheed Martin F-35 fighter jets in its proposed fiscal 2027 budget, marking a significant boost for the largest US weapons programme. The request represents an 81 per cent increase from the 47 aircraft sought in last year's budget blueprint, signalling renewed commitment to the troubled but critical Joint Strike Fighter initiative.The breakdown includes 38 F-35A conventional takeoff and landing variants for the Air Force, ten F-35B short takeoff and vertical landing jets for the Marine Corps, and 37 F-35C carrier-based models for the Navy. Of the total procurement, only 32 jets would be funded through the base budget, while the remaining 53 would require approval through reconciliation legislation currently before Congress.The request forms part of a record-breaking $1.5 trillion defence budget for fiscal 2027, with $1.15 trillion in the base budget and an additional $350 billion sought through reconciliation.
